chase_cards.name: Smeargle [Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 7 insert]
chase_cards.why: This is a chase less because of raw rarity language and more because of fit: Smeargle, the painter Pokemon, arrives through an official card magazine as a Komiya illustration with bonus-card border text. The distribution vehicle and the subject are talking to each other.

key_artists.name: Tomokazu Komiya
key_artists.why: Komiya matters because Smeargle is already a Pokemon about mark-making, painting, and copying. His loose, deformed, heavily personal visual language turns a magazine insert into an artist-to-artist card.

claims.text: The local catalog models the Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 7 insert source group as one row containing Smeargle at source index 180.
Bulbapedia says the Japanese Smeargle print was available as an Unnumbered Promotional card and was included in Volume 7 of Pokemon Card Trainers magazine, released on July 1, 2000.
Bulbapedia says the English version of this Smeargle card was released as Wizards Black Star Promo 32 through the Pokemon League in March 2001.
Bulbapedia says the Japanese print features the Crossing the Ruins symbol, indicating that it is a promotional addition to that expansion.
Bulbapedia says the bottom border text on the Japanese print reads Pokemon Card Official Magazine Trainers Vol. 7 bonus card.
Bulbapedia identifies the Smeargle card as illustrated by Tomokazu Komiya, and PokeBoon also lists Tomokazu Komiya for the Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 7 Smeargle promo.

Bulbapedia describes Tomokazu Komiya as a Pokemon Trading Card Game illustrator and Pokemon Tales book illustrator whose style is known in the Pokemon community for deformed and loosely colored images.

Bulbapedia says Komiya has illustrated Pokemon cards since the Japanese Expansion Sheet 1 expansion and often uses vibrant colors, unusual tones, exaggerated proportions, and varied brushwork to create different feelings.
Bulbapedia says Komiya contributed Smeargle and Sunflora illustrations for the 2023 Pokemon x Van Gogh art collaboration, tying his later official Pokemon work back to art-history quotation.
Bulbapedia identifies Smeargle as ドーブル Doble, a Colorless-type Basic Pokemon card with 40 HP and the Paint attack.
Bulbapedia says Smeargle is a bipedal, beagle-like Pokemon with a paintbrush-like tail and paint-like fluid, and that it uses paint to mark its territory.
Bulbapedia says Smeargle is the only known Pokemon capable of learning the move Sketch, which lets it copy moves from other Pokemon.

As judged collector texture, the Vol. 7 Smeargle insert matters because magazine distribution, Komiya's handmade style, and Smeargle's paint/Sketch identity all converge in a card about copying and mark-making.

narrative.human_title: Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 7 Smeargle: the magazine gave the painter a page
narrative.why_it_matters: This is the sort of promo that makes the early Japanese apparatus feel alive. A card magazine did not just report on the game; it carried a card into the hands of readers. And the card was Smeargle, the painter Pokemon, drawn by Tomokazu Komiya, one of the TCG's great oddball image-makers. The result feels self-aware in the best collector way: a printed magazine giving out a printed card about making marks.
not_claiming: that every Smeargle listing uses this same route

special_identification_instructions.trigger: Use when a card, listing, slab label, auction description, or agent claim says Smeargle, Pokemon Card Trainers, Trainers Vol. 7, Japanese promo, Crossing the Ruins, Wizards Promo 32, No.235, or Tomokazu Komiya.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Treat Smeargle as a reusable Pokemon/card identity. Establish the Japanese Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 7 unnumbered insert route before comparing value, rarity, or historical meaning.
steps: Confirm the card is Smeargle / ドーブル Doble and that the claimed Japanese route is Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 7 insert released July 1, 2000.
Separate the Japanese unnumbered promotional print from the English Wizards Black Star Promo 32 release through Pokemon League in March 2001.
Look for the Japanese print's bottom border text identifying Pokemon Card Official Magazine Trainers Vol. 7 bonus card.
Keep the Crossing the Ruins symbol legible as a promotional-addition marker; do not treat it as ordinary booster-set membership by itself.
Do not confuse Pokedex No. 235 or marketplace shorthand like No.235 with a printed collector number; the Japanese promo is modeled here as unnumbered.

Before spending or trade gating, require seller-controlled photos of the actual card, including the Vol. 7 border text area, expansion-symbol area, front/back, surface, edge, and slab label if graded; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.
not_claiming: that Smeargle name alone identifies the exact print
that a grading label alone resolves the route

narrative.human_title: Smeargle: Komiya draws the painter dog for the magazine crowd
narrative.why_it_matters: This card has the joy of a perfect little assignment. Smeargle is the Pokemon with the paintbrush tail and the copying move; Tomokazu Komiya is the illustrator whose TCG work often feels hand-made, bent, loose, and alive; Pokemon Card Trainers is the magazine apparatus that put the card directly into readers' hands. The result is not just a checklist promo. It is a small artifact about Pokemon learning to circulate through magazines, artists, fans, and the act of making marks.
